_: GOLDEN FIXTURES for prlint.check_pr, captured from PYTHON on 2026-10-14.
WHY: check_pr is the dispatcher - it is what makes the thirteen ported gates REACHABLE. A gate
that agrees in isolation and a dispatcher that runs them in the wrong ORDER both pass their own
tests, and only a whole-function capture catches the second.
ORDER IS PART OF THE CONTRACT: a reader meets the first problem first, and the gates run
body-declarations, then registry agreement, then housekeeping. Re-ordering would not change `ok`
and WOULD change what a lab fixes first.
MESSAGES ARE TRUNCATED TO 60 CHARS for the D23 gate only, because its message contains a live
count of files above baseline. Truncating is a deliberate weakening: it compares the stable
prefix and does NOT verify the count, which parity already checks elsewhere.

RE-CAPTURED after this unit's own docstring tripped the D23 interlock and was reworded - the first capture recorded a finding the tree no longer produces. A fixture captured while the tree was DIRTY encodes that dirt, and the comparison then fails for a reason that has nothing to do with the port.
